In a triggered condition "opponent" binds through `bindTriggerOpponent` ("choose"): it keeps only the opponents for whom the condition holds, i.e. the one owner of the dead character, bound silently with no prompt. Nothing else in the ability reads the opponent, so the trigger fires in exactly the same cases as with "opponents".

"Some opponent is the active player" is the same test as "the active player is not the controller"; the effect never reads the opponent, so the two readings fire in the same cases (the 3-seat test already covers an opponent attacking and the controller attacking).

"battle" binds the attacker only when the controller is in the battle; otherwise the engine takes the same satisfying-opponents path as the default "choose", which yields the single active player. Nothing reads the bound opponent afterwards.
